title: Find the Area of Figures with Missing Sides

sourceTextSkillAdaptation.prompt: Find the area of Figure A, the meter figure used in The Mystery Side. Use its labelled full height and upper segment to recover any length your method needs. Enter the area with m², show a non-overlapping split, and explain your expression.

originalSourceHeadings.heading: Warm-up: Notice and Wonder: Mystery Sides (10 minutes)
Activity 2: Practice with Mystery Sides (25 minutes)

originalSourceVisualAltDescriptions: 6-sided shape. Straight sides. All side lengths meet at right angles: Bottom, 4 m. Right side rises 12 m,� goes left 8 m, down 6 m, right 4 m, down question mark m.

Long description: 6-sided shape. Straight sides. All side lengths meet at right angles. Side lengths: Bottom, 4 m. Right side rises 12 m, then goes left 8 m, and down 6 m, left 4 m, and down question mark m.

learnerSourceCheck.prompt: Find the area of Figure A, the meter figure used in The Mystery Side. Use its labelled full height and upper segment to recover any length your method needs. Enter the area with m², show a non-overlapping split, and explain your expression.

supplementalLessonTeachingGuidance.sourceGoal: Let’s find the area of figures with missing side lengths.
supplementalLessonTeachingGuidance.sourceLearningGoals: Calculate the area of ungridded figures composed of rectangles, including figures with missing side lengths.
teachingSteps: Match complete horizontal and vertical spans in the centimeter warm-up.
Reject appearance as proof; recover the meter side using 12−6.
Calculate Figure A by a non-overlapping split and compare two methods.
Find Figure B’s stem width using both overhangs and match opposite vertical sides.
Write area expressions, compare/restate another method, then apply the same reasoning to the new Cool-down.
supplementalLessonTeachingGuidance.caution: Keep horizontal and vertical lengths separate; subtract every known part, avoid overlapping rectangles, and distinguish linear from square units.

firstPartyPractice.prompt: A separate right-angled figure has a full vertical height of 12 m, made from an upper 6 m segment and a missing lower segment. Find the missing length, including m. Explain the subtraction and check with addition.

independentEdulyticsCoolDown.prompt: New Edulytics task: use the separate centimeter Cool-down figure above. Find its missing inside horizontal and vertical lengths, then its area. Enter the area with cm²; show the missing-side calculations and a non-overlapping decomposition.

stageC.humanRubric: Warm-up sides are 6 cm horizontally and 7 cm vertically. The original meter diagrams in A 1 and A 2 are identical SVG bytes and the student PDF fixes all unit labels: missing 6 m and area 72 m². Figure B missing stem width 2 ft and side 4 ft gives 22 ft². Accept justified two- or three-rectangle splits without overlap. Inspect side-direction reasoning, labels, expressions, critique of Tyler, same/different-method comparison and actual MLR8 restatement. The independent Cool-down has new missing sides 6 cm and 5 cm, area 33 cm². Numerical answers do not certify explanation or discussion.

matchingScope: Exact bounded whole/decimal/fraction linear quantities with correctcm/m/ft; square-unit area quantities separately checked. No numerical answer establishes Tyler critique, side-recovery reasoning, arbitrary partition explanation or actual partner restatement.
